findings.evidence: Line 17 applies `@[expose]` to the entire file, while lines 35–37, 49–52, 61–64, 86–94, 115–119, and 125–129 provide public membership/evaluation interfaces.
findings.fix: Use `public section` without `@[expose]`; keep the definitions opaque and retain/prove the existing characteristic lemmas without relying on downstream unfolding.
findings.issue: `@[expose] public section` exposes the bodies of `ClassFunction`, both quotient constructors, the linear equivalence, and character constructors even though evaluation and membership lemmas already characterize them.

findings.evidence: Lines 35–37 are the sole public membership characterization; unlike all constructor evaluation lemmas at lines 49, 61, 86, 91, 115, and 125, it has no automation annotation.
findings.issue: The characteristic `mem_iff` lemma is not tagged `@[simp]`, so simplification does not normalize membership in `ClassFunction` to conjugation invariance once the definition is opaque.

summary: The API is usable, but all implementation bodies are unnecessarily exposed and the membership characterization is missing its normal-form annotation.
